description: Detect a worker session that dies on its first API turn from its own transcript and propagate the real cause, so a 5-second death stops costing a 30-minute cap and stops being labelled a timeout.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: BunFile exposes a synchronous `.size` byte count (0 for a missing path) but the documented BunFile reference carries NO mtime/lastModified member, so a transcript-growth probe should compare byte length of the already-read content (or use node:fs statSync for mtime) rather than expecting a Bun mtime API. Bun explicitly directs anything node:fs covers but Bun.file does not to its near-complete node:fs implementation, and no deprecation affects readFileSync.

userStories.title: Add the pure early-death detector over a session transcript
userStories.description: As the supervisor waiting on a spawned worker, I need a pure predicate that reads the session's own transcript and reports dead-on-first-turn versus still-working, so a death whose signal is available in seconds stops being indistinguishable from work in progress.
acceptanceCriteria: A pure predicate classifies a spawned session as dead-on-first-turn from its transcript alone: a transcript whose byte size has not grown across the floor window AND whose last assistant entry is a transient API error reports early-death, while a still-growing transcript, or one whose last assistant entry is normal work, reports still-working. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts -t "classifies a frozen transcript whose last assistant entry is an API error as dead-on-first-turn"]

The detector is driven against a REAL healthy-planner fixture (about 70 entries, roughly 256 KB, tool_use blocks, still growing between samples) and reports still-working, so the predicate is proven against both fixtures and not the dead one alone. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts -t "classifies a still-growing multi-entry transcript with tool_use work as still-working"]

The extracted cause text is the transcript's last assistant entry verbatim enough for a reader to see the upstream error (e.g. the 529 Overloaded line), not a synthesized label. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts -t "extracts the last assistant entry as the cause text"]
The transcript path is resolved through the existing shared resolver rather than a second path resolver. [oracle: grep -q 'transcriptPathForSession' src/supervisor/early-death.ts]

The probe resolves the transcript under an injected Claude config root that is NOT the homedir default, written to a real tmpdir, so a CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR environment (measured live) cannot make the detector read a permanently stale ~/.claude/projects directory and never fire. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts -t "resolves the transcript under an injected claudeDir that is not the homedir default"]

The floor window is a named constant or a cap-relative derivation, and is proven far below BOTH the 30-minute host cap and the 60-minute container cap, so no cap is hardcoded. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts -t "derives a floor far below both the 30-minute host cap and the 60-minute container cap"]

An absent or unreadable transcript reports still-working rather than early-death, so a resolver miss can never fabricate a death. [oracle: bun test ./test/supervisor/dispatch-early-death.test.ts -t "reports still-working when the transcript is absent or unreadable"]
